title: stochastic-pad-tradeoff-scheduler: latency-aware probabilistic batching to minimize padding waste
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation:
Current length-based bucketing approaches give deterministic bins which minimize padding at steady state but cause poor latency for small, bursty workloads and introduce sharp decision boundaries that encourage cache thrash and kernel-choice oscillation. This PR introduces the 'stochastic pad tradeoff scheduler' (SPTS): a probabilistic grouping heuristic that intentionally mixes sequence-length cohorts with tunable bias to trade a small, controlled amount of padding for improved tail-latency and KV-cache stability.

Summary of changes (single-string description with sections):
- New runtime scheduler component: runtime/scheduler/stochastic_pad_scheduler.py (Python scheduler glue + C++ bindings). Implements a length-aware probabilistic sampler that emits batch group decisions with a confidence-driven mixing parameter (pad_amortization_alpha).
- Kernel hinting: scheduler now annotates batch descriptors with preferred kernel_variant tags (e.g. attention_tiled_v2) to influence the kernel selection layer when multiple kernel backends are compatible. Added small API to runtime/kernel_selector to accept scheduler hints.
- KV cache prefetch prioritization: runtime/kv/cache_prefetcher.cc updated to use per-slot access frequency estimators to delay low-value prefill for batches with high mixing probability; reduces KV eviction churn.
- Continuous batching integration: the continuous_batcher now exposes preemption_threshold_ms and amortization_window_ms knobs so SPTS can decide to accept cross-length mixing rather than queuing for an exact bucket.
- Tests and benchmarks: runtime/tests/test_stochastic_scheduler.py, benchmarks/benchmark_pad_tradeoff.yml, docs/perf/stochastic-pad-scheduler.md.

Design highlights and parameters:
- pad_amortization_alpha (0..1): 0 = deterministic bucketing, 1 = fully randomized mixing. Default tuned to 0.18 for production workloads based on internal traces.
- amortization_window_ms: time window in which small padding is amortized vs. queuing latency (default 40ms).
- preemption_threshold_ms: how long continuous-batcher will wait for preferred-length cohorts before preempting and forming a mixed batch (default 8ms).
- Kernel hinting: scheduler tags batches with kernel_hint: ["fast_mem_attn", "tiled_attn_v2", "fp16_pack"], the kernel selector uses these heuristics to bias device-specific kernel choice.

Why this is different from plain bucketing: the probabilistic decision smooths bucket boundaries, which reduces the number of times the runtime flips between kernel variants for near-boundary sequences and reduces short-lived KV cache allocations. In our traces this yields a lower 99th percentile latency and a meaningful reduction in mean token cost because amortized padding is usually less than the eviction and cold-kernel penalties that deterministic bucketing incurred.

Small illustrative pseudocode of the core decision (included inline for reviewers):

for incoming_request in queue.incoming():
    l = incoming_request.sequence_length
    preferred_bucket = bucket_for_length(l)
    p_mix = mix_probability_for_length(l, pad_amortization_alpha)
    if random() < p_mix and queue.has_cohort_of(preferred_bucket +- delta):
        group = compose_mixed_batch(preferred_bucket, nearby_bucket)
    else:
        group = wait_for_exact_bucket(preferred_bucket, amortization_window_ms)
    annotate group with kernel_hint based on predicted seq-len distribution
    emit group to batcher

Bench numbers (summary):
- Internal offline microbench on mixed web workload: mean token cost -6.1%, 95th latency -4.3%, 99th latency -2.8% (alpha=0.18, amortization_window=40ms).
- Stress test with high-burst small-requests: observed tail-latency improvement of ~9% vs deterministic bucketing with similar throughput.

Backward-compat and rollout plan:
- Default parameters keep behavior close to existing bucketing (alpha small) so safe-by-default.
- Feature gated behind runtime flag `spts.enabled` and rollout via console per-cluster.
- Suggested rollout steps in docs/perf/stochastic-pad-scheduler.md: canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with KV cache metric tracking and kernel-variant oscillation alert.

Review conversation (condensed into single string):
- Diego Alvarez (review): "Nice approach — mixing seems promising. Two asks: (1) add microbench across different model sizes (7B/13B/70B) to ensure kernel_hint doesn't bias poorly; (2) ensure scheduler doesn't grow memory for very long seqs when mixing with short ones."
- Author (Maya): "Added additional bench harness (benchmarks/benchmark_pad_tradeoff.yml) that runs 7B/13B/70B profiles and tightened kernel_hint fallbacks. Also added max_mixed_seq_ratio clamp to avoid growth."
- Priya Nair (review): "Can you add a safety limit for KV prefill (we saw a regression in a staging run)? Recommend prefill budget per-GPU."
- Author: "Added per-device prefetch_budget and a soft-fail path to skip prefill if budget exceeded. See runtime/kv/cache_prefetcher.cc changes. Re-ran staging, no regressions."
- Jonas Berg (approve): "Tests + perf look solid. Love the rollout plan and the test coverage on kernel oscillation metrics."
- CI: initial run had a flaky test on Windows build bot (unrelated). Re-run succeeded.
- Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI. Merge note references ENG-2319 and ENG-2345.

Notes for maintainers and follow-ups:
- Consider exposing a telemetry metric `scheduler.pad_amortization_alpha` per-cluster to correlate with cost; included in docs runbook.
- Next PR idea: add online adaptation of alpha using a small control loop that watches kernel-variant oscillation and tail-latency.

Release notes (short):
- Added stochastic pad tradeoff scheduler to reduce padding waste and tail-latency by probabilistically mixing sequence-length cohorts. Feature is feature-gated and off by default. See docs/perf/stochastic-pad-scheduler.md for rollout guidance.
